newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: RUGBY UNION-RACIST SLUR ROW ROCKS S. AFRICA.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-RACIST SLUR ROW ROCKS S. AFRICA.

text.p: South African rugby union's governing body SARFU is to hold an emergency meeting on Wednesday to investigate charges of overt racism in its top ranks, officials said.
The country's rugby world was in a furore on Tuesday over the allegations, backed up by a tape-recording of racial slurs allegedly uttered by a senior official of the national squad, the Springboks.

Newspaper reports carried what they said were verbatim transcripts of the offensive remarks and named the team official under fire. They said the recording, in which an Afrikaans speaker is heard repeatedly swearing and insulting blacks, had been made without his knowledge.
The reports offered no conclusive proof of the speaker's identity.

Rian Oberholzer, head of the South African Rugby Football Union, also declined to comment on the contents of the tape, saying he had not been given a copy. Excerpts of the recording were broadcast on South African television on Monday evening.
"The executive committee is meeting in Johannesburg at 2 p.m. tomorrow (Wednesday) and (Springboks coach) Andre Markgraaff will be present at the meeting.
"These allegations will be investigated and if there is any truth in them action will be taken," Oberholzer said.

Radio reports on Tuesday said the official who allegedly made the taped comments could be fired from his top post by Thursday if the Union's investigation finds him responsible for the racist remarks.
